claims.text: A tailored multi-element high-entropy alloy electrocatalyst will have greater HER and HOR catalytic activity than conventional Pt-based systems.
A tailored multi-element high-entropy alloy electrocatalyst will have greater HER and HOR durability than conventional Pt-based systems.
Conventional Pt-based and simple Pt-alloy electrocatalysts exhibit high catalytic activity.
Conventional Pt-based and simple Pt-alloy electrocatalysts suffer from cost issues.
Conventional Pt-based and simple Pt-alloy electrocatalysts suffer from durability issues.
Incorporating multiple active elements at controlled ratios can tune the catalyst's electronic structure.
Incorporating multiple active elements at controlled ratios can tune surface energetics.
Increased alloy compositional complexity modulates the d-band center.
Increased alloy compositional complexity stabilizes the active surface against corrosion.
A balanced multi-element composition decreases hydrogen adsorption energy.
A balanced multi-element composition enhances corrosion resistance.
Decreasing hydrogen adsorption energy improves HER and HOR catalytic activity.
Enhanced corrosion resistance improves operational stability.
The proposed HEA catalyst will exhibit lower HER and HOR overpotentials than traditional Pt-based catalysts.
The proposed HEA catalyst will exhibit higher HER and HOR current densities than traditional Pt-based catalysts.
The proposed HEA catalyst will exhibit significantly improved durability during extended operation relative to traditional Pt-based catalysts.
The proposed HEA design is applicable to standard HER and HOR testing in acidic media.
The proposed HEA design is applicable to standard HER and HOR testing in alkaline media.
Changes in operating parameters could alter the effectiveness of the HEA design.
